stem: A client develops sudden intense unilateral eye pain, a red eye, blurred vision, and nausea. Which condition should the nurse suspect?
rationale: The National Eye Institute identifies sudden intense eye pain, nausea, red eye, and blurry vision as warning symptoms of angle-closure glaucoma and directs people with these symptoms to seek immediate medical care. Acute angle closure results from rapid obstruction of aqueous outflow with a sudden rise in intraocular pressure. Primary open-angle glaucoma is generally a chronic condition rather than this abrupt painful syndrome, while presbyopia and uncomplicated dry-eye disease do not produce this acute combination.
educational_objective: Recognize the sudden painful visual and systemic symptom pattern of acute angle-closure glaucoma as an ocular emergency.
source_organization: National Eye Institute (NEI), National Institutes of Health
source_locator: Section 'When to get help right away': angle-closure glaucoma can cause sudden intense eye pain, nausea, red eye, and blurry vision; page directs the client to a doctor or emergency room immediately
source_claim_supported: Sudden intense eye pain, nausea, red eye, and blurry vision are warning symptoms of angle-closure glaucoma requiring immediate medical attention.
